claims.text: Incorporating a nanoscale, thermally stable solid-lubricant additive into CoCrFeNi will form a durable, low-shear tribofilm.
The additive-induced tribofilm will reduce friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The additive-induced tribofilm will reduce wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The solid-lubricant additive will redistribute during sliding.
Redistribution of the additive will produce a continuous, lubricious tribofilm at the sliding interface.
The additive will facilitate in situ formation and maintenance of a low-shear-strength surface film.
The low-shear-strength film will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will lower friction and mitigate wear throughout the stated temperature range.
The modified alloy will have a continuously lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi over the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi over the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits higher friction than the proposed modified alloy.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits variable wear behavior, particularly as temperature increases.
The proposed effect applies under moderate sliding loads in a controlled, moderately oxidizing environment.
Performance may differ under extreme loads or highly oxidative atmospheres.
The magnitude of friction and wear improvement may depend on additive dispersion and its interaction with operating conditions.
